HMLR_BOUNDARY_WORD_NO_SPECIAL_LAW_MEANING
The word boundary has no special meaning in law.
HMLR_TWO_BOUNDARY_SENSES
A boundary may be discussed as a legal boundary or a physical boundary.
HMLR_LEGAL_BOUNDARY_INVISIBLE_LINE
A legal boundary is an imaginary or invisible line dividing ownerships.
HMLR_LEGAL_BOUNDARY_NO_THICKNESS
A legal boundary is an exact line with no thickness or width.
HMLR_LEGAL_BOUNDARY_RARELY_PRECISE
The exact legal boundary is rarely identified precisely on the ground or in deeds.
HMLR_LEGAL_BOUNDARY_NOT_OS
The legal boundary is not shown on Ordnance Survey mapping.
HMLR_DISPUTE_COURT_OR_TRIBUNAL
A disputed exact boundary can ultimately be determined only by a court or the Land Registration division of the First-tier Tribunal.
HMLR_PHYSICAL_BOUNDARY_VISIBLE
A physical boundary is a visible feature such as a fence, wall or hedge.
HMLR_PHYSICAL_MAY_COINCIDE
A physical feature may coincidentally follow the legal boundary.
HMLR_LEGAL_LINE_WITHIN_OR_SIDE
A legal boundary may run within a structure, along one side, or include adjoining road or stream land.
HMLR_HEDGE_MOVEMENT
Living boundary structures such as hedges can move or spread over time.
HMLR_OS_LINE_FEATURE_EXISTED
An OS map line indicates that a feature existed in that position subject to survey limitations.
HMLR_SURVEY_PRECISION_DEPENDS_ACCURACY
The precision recordable on a plan depends on the accuracy of the underlying survey.
HMLR_ALL_SURVEYS_HAVE_TOLERANCES
Even modern high-accuracy surveys operate within defined tolerances.
HMLR_LEGAL_POSITION_WHOLE_CONVEYANCE
The legal boundary depends on the relevant conveyance or transfer read as a whole, including its plan.
HMLR_EXTRINSIC_EVIDENCE_IF_UNCLEAR
If a plan is unclear to a reasonable layperson, a court may consider extrinsic evidence and historic physical features.
HMLR_IDENTIFICATION_ONLY_NOT_DECISIVE
A statement that a plan is for identification only does not settle the boundary question.
HMLR_REASONABLE_BUYER_TEST
The interpretive question is what a reasonable layperson would think was bought.
HMLR_SUBJECTIVE_INTENT_IRRELEVANT
The parties' subjective intentions, beliefs and assumptions are irrelevant to that interpretation.
HMLR_GENERAL_BOUNDARIES_MAJORITY
The great majority of registered titles show only general boundaries.
HMLR_FIRST_REG_NO_DETAILED_BOUNDARY_ENQUIRY
First registration is completed without detailed enquiries into the precise legal boundary.
HMLR_TITLE_PLAN_REASONABLE_INTERPRETATION
A title plan reflects a reasonable interpretation of deeds against OS detail and adjoining registrations.
HMLR_GENERAL_BOUNDARY_NO_STANDARD_TOLERANCE
No standard tolerance, measurement or ratio links a title-plan general boundary to the legal boundary.
HMLR_GENERAL_RULE_NO_QUANTITY_LIMIT
Case law says there is no limit to the quantity of land that may fall within the general-boundaries rule.
HMLR_FIXED_BOUNDARY_SUPERSEDED
The former fixed-boundary procedure has been superseded by determined-boundary provisions.
HMLR_FIXED_BOUNDARY_RARE_EXPENSIVE
Fixed-boundary registration was expensive and only a handful were completed.
HMLR_TWO_PRECISION_ROUTES
More precise registration may use a boundary agreement or a determined-boundary application.
HMLR_ADJOINER_AGREEMENT_ROUTE1
A boundary agreement always requires adjoining-owner agreement.
HMLR_ADJOINER_AGREEMENT_ROUTE2
A determined-boundary application will almost invariably also require adjoining-owner agreement.
HMLR_FENCE_CONSTRUCTION_NO_OWNERSHIP_RULE
Fence-post or rail orientation has no general legal foundation as proof of ownership.
HMLR_MAINTENANCE_COVENANT_NOT_OWNERSHIP
A covenant to maintain a wall or fence does not by itself confer ownership.
HMLR_UNKNOWN_FEATURE_PARTY_BOUNDARY
Where ownership or maintenance cannot be determined, the feature is generally best regarded as a party boundary.
HMLR_ALTERATION_NEEDS_NEIGHBOUR_AGREEMENT
Alteration or replacement of a boundary feature should be agreed with adjoining owners.
HMLR_REGISTER_ONLY_SPECIFIC_DEED_INFO
The register records boundary ownership or maintenance only when specifically referred to in lodged deeds.
HMLR_T_MARK_REGISTER_OPTIONS
Referenced T marks may be reproduced, described verbally, or linked to a filed deed plan.
HMLR_UNREFERENCED_T_MARK_NO_FORCE
A T mark not referred to in deed text has no special force or meaning in law.
HMLR_PARTY_WALL_WORKS_NOT_OWNERSHIP
The Party Wall etc Act regulates works but generally does not determine land ownership.
HMLR_ACCRETION_GRADUAL_IMPERCEPTIBLE
Accretion and diluvion apply to gradual and imperceptible natural water-boundary changes.
HMLR_WATER_BOUNDARY_FOLLOWS_NATURAL_CHANGE
A land boundary normally follows a natural progressive change in a non-tidal watercourse.
HMLR_SUDDEN_FLOOD_EXCEPTION
A sudden substantial permanent diversion does not move the boundary under the accretion doctrine.
HMLR_MANMADE_CHANGE_EXCEPTION
Man-made changes do not move the boundary under the accretion doctrine.
HMLR_TITLE_PLAN_DOES_NOT_OVERRIDE_ACCRETION
A title plan's depicted line does not prevent natural gain or loss under accretion and diluvion.
